title: Isaiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 13
description: Ten questions on Isaiah 13: the burden of Babylon, the day of Yahweh, the Medes stirred up, and a city left to wild animals.

questions.text: Isaiah 13 is called the burden of which place?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 introduces the chapter as the burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw.

questions.text: Where does verse 2 say to set up a banner?
questions.explanation: Verse 2 says to set up a banner on the bare mountain, lift up the voice and wave the hand.

questions.text: Who is mustering the army for the battle?
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says that Yahweh of Armies is mustering the army for the battle.

questions.text: In verse 8, the people in pain are compared to whom?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says pangs and sorrows will seize them, and they will be in pain like a woman in labor.

answers.text: A bird caught in a snare

questions.text: What will happen to the sun in the day of Yahweh?
questions.explanation: Verse 10 says the sun will be darkened in its going out, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.

answers.text: It will be darkened in its going out
It will stand still in the sky

questions.text: Verse 12 says people will be made more rare than what?
questions.explanation: Verse 12 says, "I will make people more rare than fine gold, even a person than the pure gold of Ophir."

questions.text: In verse 14, those who flee are compared to which animals?
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says they will be like a hunted gazelle and like sheep that no one gathers, each fleeing to his own land.

answers.text: A lion and a bear robbed of her cubs
A hunted gazelle and sheep that no one gathers
An ox and a donkey without a master

questions.text: Whom will Yahweh stir up against Babylon?
questions.explanation: Verse 17 says, "Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them," a people who will not value silver or delight in gold.

questions.text: Babylon's overthrow is compared to that of which cities?
questions.explanation: Verse 19 says Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, will be like when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

questions.text: According to verses 20-21, what will become of Babylon?
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 say it will never be inhabited; wild animals of the desert will lie there and its houses will be full of jackals.

answers.text: It will be rebuilt by shepherds
It will become a city of refuge
The Arabian will pitch his tents inside it
